name: Herdr Console
description: Inspect local Herdr workspaces and tmux sessions, read panes, send input, and receive Cindy notifications or automation triggers from Herdr events.
whenToUse: Use to inspect local Herdr agents and their panes, send prompts or input, wait for agent states, manage local Herdr and tmux panes, or bridge Herdr events into Cindy.

herdr_state.description: List Herdr workspaces, tabs, panes, and agents, including status, working directories, and titles.

herdr_read.description: Read pane or agent terminal output. Use visible for the current screen, recent for the latest lines, or recent_unwrapped for unwrapped log lines.

herdr_prompt.description: Prompt a Herdr agent and optionally wait for idle, working, blocked, done, or unknown. A blocked target receives no prompt.

herdr_send.description: Send text or keys to a Herdr pane. Use Herdr key names such as enter, ctrl+h, or shift+tab.

herdr_wait.description: Wait for an agent state or for pane output matching the supplied text.

herdr_control.description: Manage Herdr workspaces, tabs, panes, and Git worktrees. Close only when the user explicitly requests it.

herdr_notify.description: Show a notification in the Herdr terminal interface.

herdr_events.description: Check, start, or stop a Herdr event subscription, or wait for an event.

herdr_automation_setup.description: Create a Cindy automation triggered by blocked or done events, optionally linked to an existing session. Returns the automation ID and webhook address.

herdr_call.description: Call a Herdr socket API method by its full name and parameters. Calls can change Herdr state.

tmux_state.description: List local tmux sessions and panes with commands, working directories, sizes, and active state. When tmux is unavailable, return available=false and a hint.

tmux_read.description: Read the visible tmux pane or the most recent N lines, including scrollback.

tmux_send.description: Send literal text or named keys to the selected tmux pane.
